mechanism_narrative: A lower level of the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, as it reflects an accommodative monetary policy that lowers the discount rate for equity valuation and stimulates corporate investment.
failure_condition: The Rank IC for FEDFUNDS as a predictor of 20-day SPX returns is less than 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS and 20-day returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05) in a rolling 5-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 5.0% signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE exceeds 5.0% over the next 5 trading days, or the Rank IC for UNRATE as a predictor of 5-day returns is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in residential construction (HOUST) and consumer spending (RSAFS) signals a broad-based weakening in demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint decline in HOUST and RSAFS (both down > 0.5% from prior month) does not produce negative 20-day SPX returns in at least 60% of cases, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a period of strong industrial production growth (INDPRO > 115), the supply chain is robust and corporate margins are stable, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX returns are not positive in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO exceeds 115 over the next 60 trading days, or the Rank IC for INDPRO in this regime is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate above 4.5% signals a restrictive monetary policy that increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate investment, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5%, or the Rank IC for FEDFUNDS as a predictor of 20-day returns is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A higher level of employment growth (PAYEMS) is associated with stronger consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The Rank IC for PAYEMS as a predictor of 20-day SPX returns is less than 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or the correlation between PAYEMS and 20-day returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion (as indicated by high real GDP growth), consumer demand is robust but nearing saturation, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days due to profit-taking and valuation compression.
failure_condition: SPX returns are not negative in more than 60% of periods when GDPC1 exceeds 11600 over the next 60 trading days, or the Rank IC for GDPC1 in this regime is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO) and a rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a weakening supply chain and labor market, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint decline in INDPRO and rise in UNRATE (INDPRO down > 0.5% and UNRATE up > 0.3pp from prior month) does not produce negative 20-day SPX returns in at least 60% of cases, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03.
